text: Good API design makes software easier to use and maintain. When you build REST APIs, you should create clear and meaningful endpoints that show what each resource does. Always return the correct status codes, such as 200 for success or 404 when something is not found, so developers understand what happened. Good documentation is also essential because it helps others learn how to use your API quickly. Finally, you should plan for versioning from the start, for example by adding /v1/ to your URLs. This way, you can improve your API without breaking existing applications that depend on it.
